fields.Frequency: ~2–3 new VMI vendors/year; 12 vendors reviewed annually
fields.Participants: VP Supply Chain, Category Manager, VP Merchandising, Vendor
fields.Trigger: New VMI vendor onboarding; annual VMI agreement renewal

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-flag of "settlement: standard PO-based, 3-way match per W7" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "auto-create PO upon BuildRight approval or auto-approve per threshold" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-377 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Operations (PA-45.2).)
- operational: VP Supply Chain review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Parameter accuracy**: Incorrect min/max levels lead to either stockouts (too low) or excess inventory (too high); requires demand history analysis for accurate parameter setting
- **Vendor capability**: Not all vendors have EDI/API capability for VMI; smaller vendors may need manual data sharing (email spreadsheets)
System Touchpoints: - VMI parameter configuration in procurement/inventory module (W1934.2)
- Automated data sharing API setup (W1934.2)
- Integration with W36 (vendor onboarding) for vendor setup
Time Estimate: - ~4–6 weeks per vendor setup (1–2 weeks negotiation/configuration + the 4-week pilot test cycle)

steps.activity: VP Supply Chain negotiates VMI agreement with vendor: (a) scope: which SKUs are VMI-managed, which locations (DCs, stores, or both), (b) inventory parameters: minimum stock level, maximum stock level, reorder point, reorder quantity per SKU per location, (c) data sharing: BuildRight provides daily stock levels, sales data, forecast; vendor manages replenishment decisions, (d) service level: target fill rate ≥ 97%, lead time commitment, (e) ownership: VMI stock is BuildRight-owned (unlike consignment), vendor manages replenishment but BuildRight owns inventory upon receipt, (f) settlement: standard PO-based, 3-way match per W7

System configuration: (a) VMI flag set on applicable SKUs in item master, (b) VMI parameters per SKU per location: min/max/ROP/ROQ, (c) data sharing schedule: daily automated stock/sales feed to vendor, (d) auto-replenishment: vendor-generated replenishment suggestions auto-create PO upon BuildRight approval or auto-approve per threshold, (e) auto-confirmation: GR auto-confirmed against VMI ASN within tolerance

Test cycle: (a) run 4-week VMI pilot with vendor for 1 DC, (b) measure: fill rate, stockout frequency, overstock instances, GR accuracy, (c) adjust parameters based on pilot results, (d) roll out to all applicable locations

fields.Volume: ~300 VMI SKUs × ~204 locations (4 DCs + 200 stores) = ~61,200 data points/day

workflows.name: VMI Data Sharing & Demand Signal Transmission

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review data accuracy" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-377 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Operations (PA-45.2).)
- operational: System review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data latency**: If POS inventory deduction is delayed (per POS-013, < 30 sec), VMI data may be slightly stale; acceptable for daily batch but not for real-time VMI
- **Data volume**: 61,200 data points/day for 12 vendors is manageable but requires automated processing
System Touchpoints: - Automated VMI data extraction and packaging (W1935.1)
- API/EDI transmission with logging (W1935.2)
- Integration with W31 (demand forecasting) for forecast data

steps.activity: System compiles daily VMI data package per vendor: (a) current stock level per SKU per location, (b) daily sales (units) per SKU per location, (c) in-transit stock (VMI POs not yet received), (d) pending returns, (e) forecast data (if available from W31 demand forecast), (f) promotional calendar impact (upcoming promos affecting VMI SKUs)

System transmits data to vendor: (a) preferred: API/EDI transmission directly to vendor's VMI system, (b) fallback: automated email with CSV/Excel attachment, (c) transmission log maintained for audit trail

VP Supply Chain monitors data transmission: (a) daily check: did all 12 vendors receive data successfully?, (b) failed transmission: retry within 2 hours, (c) vendor feedback: any data quality issues reported?, (d) monthly: review data accuracy (do vendor's stock numbers match BuildRight's?)

fields.Trigger: Vendor generates replenishment suggestion based on VMI data

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews VMI data and generates replenishment order" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "BuildRight system processes ASN" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document exception resolution" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-377 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Operations (PA-45.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Overstocking risk**: Vendor has incentive to push more stock (ensures shelf presence); min/max parameters and spending caps prevent excess; mitigated by CTL-377 (controlled execution — Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Operations (PA-45.2))

- **Auto-approval risk**: If parameters are set too loosely, system may auto-approve excessive replenishment; requires periodic parameter review; mitigated by CTL-377 (controlled execution — Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Operations (PA-45.2))
System Touchpoints: - ASN-to-PO auto-creation (W1936.2)
- Tolerance-based auto-approval (W1936.2)
- Integration with W2A (auto-replenishment) for PO creation
Time Estimate: - Automated for standard replenishment; 15–30 min per exception

steps.activity: Vendor reviews VMI data and generates replenishment order: (a) vendor's VMI system calculates replenishment needs based on min/max parameters and recent sales, (b) vendor creates ASN (Advance Shipping Notice) with: SKU, qty, ship date, estimated arrival, (c) ASN transmitted to BuildRight system via API/EDI

BuildRight system processes ASN: (a) auto-create PO from ASN (within VMI agreement parameters), (b) validate: (i) total PO value within VMI agreement spending limit, (ii) SKU qty within min/max parameters, (iii) delivery schedule aligns with DC/store receiving capacity, (c) if within tolerance: auto-approve PO, (d) if outside tolerance: route to Buyer for manual review

Buyer reviews exceptions: (a) vendor suggests qty above max level: reject or approve with reason (e.g., upcoming promo), (b) vendor suggests SKUs not in VMI agreement: reject, (c) vendor suggests delivery to non-VMI location: reject, (d) document exception resolution

fields.Trigger: VMI delivery arrives at DC or store

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enter PO number" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-update of "updates stock position automatically" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-match of "matching" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **ASN accuracy**: If vendor's ASN quantities don't match actual delivery, auto-confirmation creates reconciliation issues; enforce ASN accuracy KPI in vendor scorecard
System Touchpoints: - VMI GR with auto-confirmation (W1937.2)
- 3-way match for VMI POs (W1937.3)
- Integration with W3 (DC receiving) and W18 (DSD receiving)
Time Estimate: - 15–30 min per receipt; auto-confirmation is automated

steps.activity: Receiving Clerk processes VMI delivery: (a) scan ASN barcode or enter PO number, (b) verify quantities against ASN, (c) standard goods receipt process: scan items, check condition, (d) system posts GR: (i) inventory increases at WAC (BuildRight-owned, unlike consignment), (ii) GR/IR created for 3-way match, (iii) AP liability created

Auto-confirmation: (a) if GR qty within ASN tolerance (typically ±2%), system auto-confirms receipt to vendor via API, (b) vendor's VMI system updates stock position automatically, (c) if GR qty outside tolerance: manual discrepancy resolution with vendor per W244
Invoice matching: (a) vendor invoice received, (b) system performs 3-way match: PO → GR → Invoice, (c) standard AP processing per W7

workflows.name: VMI Stock Level Monitoring & Exception Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitors VMI stock levels daily" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "VP Supply Chain reviews exceptions" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-issue of "issues identified" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-377 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Operations (PA-45.2).)
- operational: VP Supply Chain review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stockout responsibility**: When VMI SKUs stock out, BuildRight may blame vendor but vendor may cite inaccurate demand signals; clear SLA and root cause assignment needed
System Touchpoints: - VMI exception monitoring dashboard (W23)
- Automated alerts to vendor and BuildRight supply chain team (W23)
- Integration with W250 (supply chain control tower) for visibility

steps.activity: System monitors VMI stock levels daily: (a) flag SKUs below minimum level (stockout risk), (b) flag SKUs above maximum level (overstock risk), (c) flag SKUs at zero stock (immediate action needed), (d) flag SKUs with consistent above-max pattern (parameter adjustment needed)

VP Supply Chain reviews exceptions: (a) below-min: did vendor replenish? If not, escalate to vendor with SLA breach notice, (b) above-max: did vendor over-ship? Request return or adjust future orders, (c) zero stock: emergency replenishment — expedite from vendor or transfer from another location per W22

Weekly: VP Supply Chain conducts VMI exception review with Category Manager: (a) top 10 stockout SKUs by lost sales estimate, (b) top 10 overstock SKUs by excess value, (c) vendor response time to replenishment triggers, (d) adjust VMI parameters if systemic issues identified

fields.Participants: Category Manager, VP Supply Chain, Vendor
fields.Trigger: New product launch; product phase-out decision

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitor closely for first 4 weeks" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-flag of "flags SKU for phase-out in VMI agreement" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-377 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Operations (PA-45.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Initial parameter guessing**: New products have no demand history; parameters based on similar items may be inaccurate; expect 2–3 parameter adjustments in first 2 months
System Touchpoints: - VMI parameter configuration for new SKUs (W1939.1)
- SKU phase-out flag in VMI module (W1939.2)
- Integration with W315 (product lifecycle status governance)
Time Estimate: - 1–2 days per new SKU setup; 1–2 weeks per phase-out

steps.activity: New VMI product introduction: (a) Category Manager adds new SKU to VMI agreement, (b) VP Supply Chain configures VMI parameters (min/max/ROP/ROQ) based on similar product demand history, (c) initial stock: vendor ships initial fill within 2 weeks of SKU activation, (d) monitor closely for first 4 weeks: compare actual demand to parameter assumptions

VMI product phase-out: (a) Category Manager flags SKU for phase-out in VMI agreement, (b) vendor stops replenishment, (c) remaining VMI stock sold through normally (or returned to vendor per agreement), (d) once stock reaches zero: remove from VMI parameters, (e) if significant remaining stock: negotiate vendor buyback or markdown support

fields.Frequency: ~6 major promos/year; ~2–3 VMI SKUs per promo
fields.Participants: Category Manager, VP Supply Chain, Pricing Analyst, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Promotional calendar event involving VMI SKUs

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify VMI SKUs in upcoming promo per W13" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-create of "created for promo stock" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "reviews promo performance per VMI vendor" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-377 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Operations (PA-45.2).)
- operational: Category Manager review and approval gate; operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Promo stock excess**: If promo doesn't perform as expected, excess VMI stock sits in DC; vendor may not accept return; negotiate promo stock buyback clause
System Touchpoints: - VMI promotional parameter override (W1940.2)
- Promotional VMI stock tracking (W1940.3)
- Integration with W13 (promotions) and W57 (promo stock allocation)
Time Estimate: - 1–2 days pre-promo planning; 2–3 days post-promo reconciliation

steps.activity: Category Manager plans VMI promotional stock: (a) identify VMI SKUs in upcoming promo per W13, (b) estimate incremental demand: historical promo lift × base demand, (c) communicate to vendor: (i) promo dates, (ii) expected volume increase, (iii) required pre-positioning: extra stock in DCs 2 weeks before promo, (d) negotiate vendor contribution to promotional cost per PUR-026

Vendor adjusts VMI replenishment: (a) vendor pre-ships promotional stock to DCs, (b) VMI system temporarily overrides max stock level for promo period, (c) additional PO created for promo stock (separate from auto-replenishment), (d) promo stock received and staged for rapid deployment to stores

Post-promo: (a) VP Supply Chain reconciles promo VMI stock: (i) promo qty sold vs. promo qty received, (ii) unsold promo stock: return to vendor or sell at regular price, (b) Category Manager reviews promo performance per VMI vendor, (c) VMI parameters reset to standard levels

fields.Participants: VP Supply Chain, Category Manager, Vendor

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-compile of "compiles quarterly VMI scorecard per vendor" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review VMI parameter adequacy" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-calculate of "calculate VMI program ROI" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-377 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Operations (PA-45.2).)
- operational: VP Supply Chain review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor complacency**: VMI vendors meeting minimum SLA may not strive for improvement; link VMI performance to overall vendor scorecard and business allocation decisions
System Touchpoints: - VMI scorecard dashboard (W1941.1)
- Integration with W44 (vendor performance review) for consolidated scorecard
Time Estimate: - 1 day/quarter scorecard; 12–24 hours/quarter vendor meetings; 2–3 days/year program review

steps.activity: VP Supply Chain compiles quarterly VMI scorecard per vendor: (a) fill rate: % of VMI SKUs at or above minimum stock level, (b) stockout rate: % of VMI SKUs at zero stock, (c) overstock rate: % of VMI SKUs above maximum stock level, (d) replenishment lead time: average days from stock signal to delivery, (e) ASN accuracy: % of receipts matching ASN within tolerance, (f) GR accuracy: % of deliveries with quantity discrepancies, (g) promo stock compliance: did vendor deliver promo stock on time and in full?

VP Supply Chain meets with each VMI vendor: (a) present scorecard results, (b) discuss improvement areas, (c) set targets for next quarter, (d) review VMI parameter adequacy: do min/max levels need adjustment?, (e) discuss new product introductions or phase-outs planned

Annual: VP Supply Chain evaluates VMI program effectiveness: (a) compare VMI vendor performance to non-VMI vendor performance (fill rate, stockout, inventory turns), (b) calculate VMI program ROI: (reduced procurement labor + reduced stockouts) vs. (VMI system cost + vendor data sharing infrastructure), (c) recommend VMI program expansion or contraction
